artist_profile: Chicago indie-rock five-piece on this tour: Julia Steiner (lead vocal + guitar, centre), Dave Sagan (lead guitar, stage left, on a wedge), Sean Neumann (bass + BVs, stage right), Marcus Nuccio (drums, on ears) and touring player Andy 'Red' PK (pedal steel + guitar + acoustic, riser stage left). Sixth record 'Singin' to an Empty Chair' (New West, Feb 2026) is the tour: Sagan's guitar 'from gently probing to outright inferno' (Paste), slide into thick distortion, fingerpicked acoustic openings that build to full band (DIY Mag), and a Sept 2026 Tiny Desk that spent a third of the set on one long song — the jam sections are real. Steiner's voice is light and sweet (NPR) and has to sit over a distorted lead and a steel. Mix priority: Julia intelligible over the wall, Dave's lead cutting in the 1k lane not the top, steel as colour, a kick/snare that drives.

Humid but well under the 90% inversion line: HF carries, so baked peaks are trimmed but no channel needs an HF rescue and no channel gets an HF boost. Everyone but Dave is on the band's own IEM rack; one house wedge downstage left.

reconciliation: No web↔KB disagreements on the units that have a KB row (Beta 91A, 421-U, SM57, SM58, V7, piezo acoustic, sampling pad, bass DI lane rule) — all AGREE.
Nine units THIN — touring mics with no KB row (NXN2, NXN6 ×3, NXN5, Karma K-Micro, PRO 37, SM27 ×2, MD409). Brian: build from the web findings and add the rows.
kb_writeback: NEW ROW — Shure Nexadyne NXN2: supercardioid dual-transducer kick, 20 Hz–16 kHz, −66 dBV/Pa, built-in 450 Hz scoop + broad 4.5 kHz lift (Mix). Tendency: no click boost, no cut at 450.
NEW ROW — Shure Nexadyne NXN6: supercardioid tom/snare, 50 Hz–16 kHz, −61 dBV/Pa, wide smooth ~6 kHz presence (Mix). Tendency: attack is baked, trim don't boost.
NEW ROW — Shure Nexadyne NXN5: supercardioid amp mic, 50 Hz–16 kHz, presence peak centred 6 kHz (Mix, PSW). Tendency: trim 6k on bright sources (steel).
NEW ROW — Karma K-Micro Silver Bullet: electret SDC, 20–20k, dip ~2 kHz, ~7 dB peak ~6.5 kHz (SOS). Hat/snare-bottom class. Tendency: trim 6.5k, never cut 2k.
NEW ROW — Audio-Technica PRO 37: SDC, 30 Hz–15 kHz, 141 dB SPL, big 7 kHz hype, roll-off above ~12k (Gearspace, RecordingHacks). Tendency: −6 at 7k on cymbals.
NEW ROW — Shure SM27: LDC, 40 Hz–20 kHz, 148 dB SPL, 9.5 dBA, flat with slight presence/air; rolloff 80/115, −15 pad (RecordingHacks). Cab and overhead use; nothing baked to trim.
NEW ROW — Sennheiser MD 409: ~5 dB bump 100–200 Hz, dip <100, even to ~15k; NOT the e609 (which adds a broad 5k lift) (Xaudia measurements). Tendency: trim the low bump, mids honest.
eq-starting-points — front + rear mic on one open-back cab: rear leg polarity-flipped, LPF ~2k, body-only lane 70–250, box cut ~450; front mic HPF above the rear's lane (RatBoys 09-18).
eq-starting-points — pedal steel through a 1×12 combo: wide −7@350, −4@700, trim the mic's top; Steel Guitar Forum consensus (RatBoys 09-18).

channels.name: Kick In
channels.notes: Two-mic kick with CH2 (NXN2). One signal: same VCA, blend fixed at soundcheck, sum to mono and flip one leg if it thins. Contour switch assumed OFF (flat) — if the band runs it ON, the 400 cut is already in the mic: back B3 off to −2.
channels.mic_notes: Band's Beta 91A boundary inside the shell — owns the ATTACK lane. Nominally flat with the contour off; picks up shell box 300–500. GATE (doc only): Green/FET, thr ~−28, atk 1 ms, hold 40, rel 120, range 20 — fast enough for the driving eighth-note kick, range shallow so the ring under the jam sections survives.
channels.eq_summary: Attack lane only. +3@3.5k is the beater snap a rock kick wants outdoors, placed BELOW the NXN2's baked 4.5k lift so the two clicks don't stack (Mix: NXN2 'broad boost centred at 4.5 kHz'). −7@400 is the boundary mic's documented box zone at outdoor depth. Lows flat — the NXN2 owns bottom.

channels.name: Kick Out
channels.notes: Outside/port mic on the band's short boom. Owns the BODY lane. Polarity vs CH1 checked in mono.
channels.mic_notes: Revonic dual-transducer supercardioid, 20 Hz–16 kHz. The capsule already scoops 450 Hz (built-in low-Q bandpass) and lifts 4.5 kHz (Mix real-world review) — so no box cut near 450 (it's already gone) and no click boost (it's already there). Sub reach is real: Mix heard 'a good mix of subsonic energy and attack' out front.
channels.eq_summary: Body lane. +3@60 gives the KS21 arch something to carry — cleared because the NXN2 has no baked low peak, just flat reach to 20 Hz. −4@250 clears the low-mid between the fundamental and the mic's own 450 scoop (not inside the scoop — R15). −3@4.5k trims the baked click so CH1 owns attack alone. HPF 30.

channels.name: Snare Top
channels.notes: Snare top only — no bottom mic on this list. Clip mount (band).
channels.mic_notes: NXN6 supercardioid, 50 Hz–16 kHz, a wide smooth presence rise around 6 kHz (Mix: 'about the same frequency [as the NXN5's 6 kHz] but much wider and smoother'). The crack is baked in: no B4 boost, and if it reads harsh on the open plaza trim −2@6k rather than reach for air. Mix noted minimal hat leakage on snare. GATE (doc only): Green/FET, thr ~−30, atk 0.5 ms, hold 60, rel 150, range 15 — shallow range so ghost notes in the quieter verses stay.
channels.eq_summary: Rock snare outdoors: +3@180 body (cleared — NXN6 has full low end with no baked low peak; 180 is above its 50 Hz floor and below the box), −6@400 box at outdoor depth. Top left alone because the capsule already carries the 6k crack. HPF 100.

channels.name: Hat
channels.notes: Band's electret pencil, needs 48V. Aim the capsule away from the snare.
channels.mic_notes: Karma K-Micro: electret SDC, 20 Hz–20 kHz, plot shows a DIP around 2 kHz and a ~7 dB PEAK around 6–6.5 kHz (Sound On Sound review, RecordingHacks). So the sizzle is baked — trim it — and there is no 2k cut here because the capsule already scoops that zone (R15).
channels.eq_summary: HPF 400 decisive — the hat mic on this kit is fighting snare bleed from a mic that sits low. −5@6.5k shaves the capsule's own peak so the hat doesn't turn to tizz in the open air. −6@500 is snare-body bleed. Nothing at 2k on purpose.

channels.name: Rack
channels.notes: Rim clip (band). No sizes notated — generic rack.
channels.mic_notes: Same NXN6 as the snare: baked wide 6k presence for stick attack, full lows. Mix on a rack tom: 'thick tonality with plenty of attack'. GATE (doc only): Green/FET, thr ~−32, atk 1 ms, hold 80, rel 200, range 25.
channels.eq_summary: +3@120 fundamental weight (cleared — no baked low peak). −7@400 box at outdoor depth. Attack is the capsule's — no top boost.

channels.name: Floor
channels.notes: Rim clip (band). Generic floor.
channels.mic_notes: NXN6 on a floor: Mix heard 'a big, meaty sound with good transients' — the low end is not a problem to solve, the low-mid is. GATE (doc only): Green/FET, thr ~−32, atk 1 ms, hold 100, rel 300, range 25 — slower release than the rack so the floor's decay in the slow songs doesn't chop.
channels.eq_summary: +3@80 fundamental (cleared, no baked peak there). −8@350 is the outdoor floor-tom mud cut, deeper than the rack because the shell is bigger. −3@700 rings. Top stays with the capsule.

channels.name: Ride
channels.notes: Band mounts it UNDER the ride on a short boom, capsule facing the bell from below and away from the floor tom. Mono channel, its own fader.
channels.mic_notes: PRO 37 SDC, 30 Hz–15 kHz, 141 dB SPL. The tell is a big ~7 kHz hype and a steep roll-off above ~12 kHz (Gearspace 'real opinions' thread; RecordingHacks) — users 'find themselves doing deep cuts around there, especially on cymbals'. Underhead placement hears more ping and stick than wash, and more floor-tom bleed than a true overhead (A-T ride-miking blog; DFO underhead thread). DUCK (doc only): thr ~−45, range 20 — a ducker, not a gate, so the ride tail is never chopped.
channels.eq_summary: This channel is ping and stick, not air. −6@7k sits on the capsule's baked hype (trim, never boost). −4@2.5k is stick clank on a bright ride, deeper outdoors. −6@600 is floor-tom bleed coming up from below. HPF 500.

channels.name: OH
channels.notes: ONE SM27 on a tall boom, mono, its own fader (band's call: ride and overhead are separate mono channels). Mic switches assumed FLAT / no pad — confirm at load-in; the desk HPF does the low-cut work so leave the mic's 80/115 Hz switch flat.
channels.mic_notes: SM27 LDC, 40 Hz–20 kHz, 148 dB SPL, 9.5 dBA self-noise, generally flat with a slight presence/air lift (RecordingHacks spec; AudioTechnology and Podcastage reviews). Nothing baked to fight. As a single mono overhead over a ride-plus-crash kit it's crash, hat wash and kit glue — the ride has its own mic.
channels.eq_summary: HPF 300 — this mic is cymbals and glue, the shells are all close-miked. −5@500 pulls snare/tom body bleed. −4@3k is the crash's harsh zone in the open air; no baked peak there on this mic so it's a real cut, not a trim. No top boost — 76% RH by set time and a flat capsule that already has air.

channels.name: SPD L
channels.notes: Roland SPD-SX stereo out, L leg, band's passive Radial Pro D2 (green DI). Mono channel panned hard L. No 48V. FADER 9: the template's stereo Overheads channel — Brian breaks the stereo link on the desk and runs it mono; the build only renames and EQs it.
channels.mic_notes: Passive DI on finished audio — every sample was EQ'd and compressed before it reached the pad (KB sampling-pad row). No transducer to correct, no boost available; the Pro D2 is a flat passive box with a −15 dB pad if the SPD runs hot (Radial spec). Gearspace live-sound thread on SPD-SX level: run the pad's master high and pad at the DI rather than chase gain at the desk.
channels.eq_summary: One venue-driven trim: −5@300 where the samples overlap bass and guitars on the plaza. HPF 40 so a sub-heavy sample still reaches the KS21s. Panned L; both legs identical.

channels.name: SPD R
channels.notes: Roland SPD-SX stereo out, R leg, band's passive Radial Pro D2 (green DI). Mono channel panned hard R. No 48V. FADER 10: the template's SNARE PL8 reverb return, repurposed as a mono input for this show on Brian's explicit call (band runs their own reverbs). Patcher run with --allow-protected 10; re-patch the fader's input to Local 10 on the desk.
channels.mic_notes: Passive DI on finished audio — every sample was EQ'd and compressed before it reached the pad (KB sampling-pad row). No transducer to correct, no boost available; the Pro D2 is a flat passive box with a −15 dB pad if the SPD runs hot (Radial spec). Gearspace live-sound thread on SPD-SX level: run the pad's master high and pad at the DI rather than chase gain at the desk.
channels.eq_summary: One venue-driven trim: −5@300 where the samples overlap bass and guitars on the plaza. HPF 40 so a sub-heavy sample still reaches the KS21s. Panned R; both legs identical.

channels.name: Bass DI
channels.notes: XLR out of the band's rig / DI. Ask at load-in whether it is PRE or POST the amp EQ: if POST, drop the +3@800 (the amp already voiced it — KB post-EQ DI rule) and keep the cuts. No 48V unless it turns out to be a house J48.
channels.mic_notes: Line feed — no capsule. Lane owner for everything BELOW 100 Hz and for definition (KB mic+DI rule: DI owns <100, cab mic owns above). Sean's lines are melodic and busy ('fantastic bass line' — AV Club on the new record), so definition matters more than growl. COMP (doc only): Red/VCA 4:1, atk 20 ms, rel 100 ms, 4–5 dB GR, GR target 4 — even the melodic runs out.
channels.eq_summary: −6@250 clears the low-mid so the 421 leg can own it. +3@800 is note definition on a clean DI (cleared: no transducer, nothing baked). −4@3k tames string clank and pick edge outdoors. HPF 35 — the 2×15 rig is doing sub on stage but FOH still wants fundamental through the arch.

channels.name: Bass Mic
channels.notes: Band's 421 on a short boom at the 215 rig, 1 in off the grille between dust-cap and cone edge. Bass roll-off at M (flat) assumed — if they run it at S the low-mid cut can ease to −4. Polarity vs CH11 checked in mono; the pair is ONE signal on one VCA.
channels.mic_notes: Vintage 421-U (the band's — any '421' on this list is theirs, not the house Silver Tail). 30 Hz–17 kHz with the bass tube, low-mid girth 200–400 that blooms up close, and a voiced presence rise ~4–5 kHz (Sennheiser spec, KB row). On a 2×15 the cab itself lives 30 Hz–5 kHz (Seismic 215 spec) so the 421's top is mostly grille noise.
channels.eq_summary: Lane: 100 Hz up. HPF 100 is the lane boundary handed to the DI. −7@300 is the 421's close-up bloat plus the 15s' low-mid at outdoor depth. −3@4.5k trims the baked presence rise (not a cut into a scoop). LPF 8k — nothing useful above it from two 15s.

channels.name: J Gtr
channels.notes: Julia's 410 guitar combo, centre stage, band's SM27 on a short boom. Switches flat, pad OFF unless the amp is cranked (148 dB SPL — it won't be). 48V.
channels.mic_notes: SM27 on a cab: full body, no 2–4 kHz bite (AudioTechnology: 'adds fullness without biting your head off around 2–4 kHz'; Premier Guitar review). Nothing baked to trim. The cab is four 10s: tighter, more midrange, less low end than 12s (Gearspace 10 vs 12 thread), so it is the natural owner of the TOP lane of the twin-guitar section. Julia plays rhythm under her own vocal, so this channel sits under CH20 at all times.
channels.eq_summary: Twin-guitar slot: Julia owns 2–4k jangle (4×10 + open SM27), Dave owns the 600–1.2k midrange. −7@350 mud at outdoor depth. −3@900 cedes the midrange to Dave's lead. No top cut — this channel IS the top lane. LPF 10k for fizz in the open. HPF 100.

channels.name: D Gtr Front
channels.notes: FRONT of Dave's 212 combo (stage left), band's MD409 on a short boom, on the grille toward the cone edge. Partner is CH15 (rear 57): ONE signal, same VCA, blend set at soundcheck — the 409 leads, the 57 fills. Equipboard lists his amp as a Fender Hot Rod Deluxe with a Tele/Strat and a JHS Morning Glory into a Strymon BlueSky — confirm the 212 at load-in.
channels.mic_notes: MD409 signature (Xaudia measured five units): a ~5 dB bump at 100–200 Hz and a dip below 100 Hz, otherwise even to ~15 kHz — NOT a presence-peak mic like the e609 (which adds a broad 5k lift the 409 lacks). So the warmth is baked; trim it rather than boost body, and the mids are honest so a mid boost is clean. This is the LEAD guitar: 'from gently probing to outright inferno' (Paste), slide into thick distortion, long jam sections (Tiny Desk review) — the channel needs cut in the 1k lane, not more bass.
channels.eq_summary: Owns the midrange lane of the twin-guitar section. +3@1k is lead-guitar cut-through, cleared because the 409 has no mid peak to stack on. −3@160 trims the capsule's own 100–200 bump so it doesn't pile on the rear mic's body. −3@3k cedes the top lane to Julia's 4×10. HPF 120 (the 57 owns below). LPF 9k.

channels.name: D Gtr Rear
channels.notes: REAR of Dave's open-back 212, band's SM57 on a short boom pointed at the back of the cone. POLARITY FLIP ON THIS CHANNEL — the back of the cone moves away when the front moves toward the 409, so the rear mic arrives inverted by physics (Recording magazine 'One amp, three mics'; SOS two-mic guitar tracking). Flip, sum with CH14 in mono, slide the mic until the sum is fullest. Body-only role, rides 6–10 dB under the front.
channels.mic_notes: SM57 hearing the OPEN BACK: the rear of an open cab radiates mostly low end and cabinet resonance — the highs beam out the front (Recording magazine; Marshall forum front-vs-rear). Its 6–7 kHz presence peak (KB row) is irrelevant here because the channel is low-passed. The rear mic 'can help beef up a top-heavy front-miked guitar sound' (SOS) — exactly the job under the 409 during the loud sections.
channels.eq_summary: Lane: 70–250 body, nothing else. LPF 2k keeps the rear leg out of the top where two mics on one cone would comb. −4@450 is the open-back cabinet's box resonance. No boost — the front 409 already bakes 100–200, this leg just fills under it. HPF 70.

channels.name: Acoustic
channels.notes: Andy's acoustic on the riser, stage left, through the band's DI box (plot: 'acoustic (DI box)'). No 48V unless it turns out to be a house J48. Songs open fingerpicked and build ('delicate acoustic guitars giving way to a more urgent, driving sound' — DIY Mag), so this channel carries quiet intros alone.
channels.mic_notes: Pickup/piezo-class line feed — no capsule, the transient-rich under-saddle quack is the whole problem (Radial acoustic-pickup blog; SOS 'Mixing Acoustic Guitars Live'). KB piezo rule: the 1.5–2k quack is the primary cut, plus 200–400 mud, at outdoor depth on FSQ. Folk-conservative in spirit but the numbers are FSQ-deep because there is no room to hide in.
channels.eq_summary: −7@1.8k is the piezo quack, the primary move, outdoor depth. −7@250 body mud that would smear into the bass DI. LPF 12k trims pickup hash. No boost — the fingerpicked intros want natural, and the vocal owns the presence band. HPF 100.

channels.name: Cowbell
channels.notes: Mounted stage left by Dave on a tall boom (plot). Band's 57.
channels.mic_notes: A cowbell is two clangy partials near 590 and 850 Hz (SOS synthesis reference) — that IS the instrument, so nothing is cut there. The SM57's baked peak is at 6–7 kHz, +5 to +7 (KB row), which on a cowbell is pure spike.
channels.eq_summary: HPF 250 under the partials. −5@3k is the ring harshness in the open, −4@6.5k trims the 57's own peak on the strike. LPF 10k. Partials at 590/850 left alone.

channels.name: Steel
channels.notes: Andy's 112 guitar combo on the riser, stage left, band's NXN5 on a short boom. Also his electric guitar when he switches (plot: 'STEEL/GTR') — same channel, same curve, the steel is the harder case so it sets the numbers.
channels.mic_notes: NXN5 supercardioid, 50 Hz–16 kHz, presence peak centred at 6 kHz from the grille/housing (Mix real-world review; PSW road test), with 'a little more midrange cut to counteract proximity'. Steel Guitar Forum consensus for steel through a Fender-style combo: wide cut 300–400 (boom), a dip in the 600–800 zone, and go easy on the top because the instrument already has 'tons of highs' and ice-picks on the high strings.
channels.eq_summary: −7@350 wide is the steel/combo boom at outdoor depth. −4@700 is the forum's midrange dip so the steel colours rather than honks against Dave's 1k lane. −4@6k trims the NXN5's baked peak right where the steel already ice-picks — a trim, not a cut into a scoop. LPF 10k. HPF 100.

channels.name: Sean Vox
channels.notes: Sean, stage right, tall boom with clip (plot). Band's SM58. Backing vocal under Julia; on ears.
channels.mic_notes: SM58: 50 Hz–15 kHz, bass rolled below 100 for close work, proximity +6–10 dB at 100 Hz inside 6 mm (Shure user guide), presence in the 4–6 kHz region, upper-mid spit and box when close (KB row). Cuts only. COMP (doc only): Blue/Neve 3:1, atk 10 ms, rel 150 ms, GR target 3–4.
channels.eq_summary: Cuts only. HPF 110 — the harmony slot, above Julia's 100-class HPF so his low end never crowds the lead. −6@400 box. −4@2.5k nasal/spit lane (Julia's is at 3k so the two cuts never share a frequency). −3@5k tames the 58's presence rise before it feeds back on the open plaza. No boosts.

channels.name: Julia Vox
channels.notes: Julia, centre, tall boom with clip (plot). Band's sE V7. Lead vocal, plays guitar (CH13) at the same time; on ears.
channels.mic_notes: sE V7 supercardioid dynamic: presence peak centred nearer 3 kHz than the SM58's 4–5k, a welcome dip in the sibilance zone at ~6 kHz, then an air bump above 10 kHz; smooth proximity build below 1 kHz (Sound On Sound V3/V7 review; Tape Op). A 'sweet' voice (NPR Tiny Desk copy) that has to sit over a distorted lead and a pedal steel. Cuts only — and NOTHING at 6k because the capsule already dips there (R15). COMP (doc only): Blue/Neve 3:1, atk 10 ms, rel 120 ms, GR target 4–5 — she goes from fingerpicked whisper to full band.
channels.eq_summary: Cuts only. HPF 130 — female lead, sits above the guitar she's playing. −6@300 mud/proximity. −4@3k trims the V7's own presence peak, which is also the plaza feedback zone. −3@10k eases the air bump for gain-before-feedback at 76% RH. No cut at 6k on purpose. No boosts.
